$comment: v1/presentations.batchUpdate -> POST v1/presentations/{presentationId}:batchUpdate. The requests array is Google's own, passed through as JSON (send.value json) -- every Request kind Google offers, applied ATOMICALLY: if one request is invalid, none is applied. Read from Google's discovery document 2026-11-08.
title: Batch update a Google Slides presentation
description: Apply a list of Google Slides presentation API requests to a presentation, all or none.
$idempotencyComment: batchUpdate declares no idempotency key. Whether a retry is safe depends on the requests: a replace is usually a no-op the second time, an insert is not.

config.label: Presentation ID
config.description: From presentation_create's data.presentationId, or the id in the presentation's own URL.

config.label: Requests
config.description: Google's Request objects, in order. Example: [{"replaceAllText":{"containsText":{"text":"{{name}}","matchCase":true},"replaceText":"Ada"}}].

config.label: Required revision ID
config.description: Optional. The presentation's revisionId as you last read it. If the presentation has changed since, Google refuses the whole batch with a 400 instead of applying it to content you have not seen.

outputShape.description: One reply per request, in order. Many kinds reply with an empty object.
The presentation's revision after the update; pass it to the next batch to guard it.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
